To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
nonthermally treated red mud (NTRM), produced from bauxite red mud (RM), paper sludge ash, and high-calcum fly ash, was successfully used as a partial replacement of slag cement (SC) in SC mortar.

a method was proposed for producing dried powder from red sludge with 60% water content by mixing it with paper sludge ash and high-calcum fly ash, which was confirmed to have sufficient compressive strength for use as a construction material.

a nonthermally treated dried red mud (NTRM)-slag cement mortar with 20 wt% NTRM replacement of the binder was developed, and it exhibited a compressive strength of 28.5 MPa, which is sufficient for use in sidewalks, parking lots, and bike roads.
In summary, our research is concerned with
a new method to produce NTRM powder and its use in slag cement mortar.
the development of a new method to produce dried red mud powder from RM sludge without heating, and the results indicate that NTRM can be applied as a construction material.
the development of a new method of producing dried powder from RM sludge without heating, which could be applied to the recycling of RM.

NTRM can be used in the construction industry, and the method of producing dried powder from RM sludge without heating is applicable.
this study provides the basis for a sustainable and eco-friendly method of using RM sludge as a construction material by replacing a portion of the binder.
the NTRM-mix mortar can be applied to nonstructural concrete.

NTRM can be a good alternative to cement and slag cement in the production of mortar for nonstructural applications.

the NTRM produced in this study is an alternative construction material that is suitable as a partial binder in mortar and concrete.
